answer: Verifiable Delay Cryptographic Identity Agents register by solving a puzzle bound to an unpredictable blockhash pulled from an ocean of decentralized entropy. Each solved puzzle yields a single transient key. If an agent tries to spawn thousands of sybils, the required sequential hashing time scales linearly, consuming massive CPU cycles akin to heating a cold wharf with a tiny ember. The attacker pays a heavy computational cost and forfeits the race against time.
